I presume you're using the latest version (check in
inla.upgrade(testing=TRUE))

if so, try adding

inla(..., control.fixed = list(prec.intercept = 0.01))

ie using a proper prior for the intercept. it might be that your
graph has more than one connected component, you can check with

g = inla.read.graph("graph.file")
print(g$cc$n)


otherwise, send data and code so I can run it here...

> >

second thought!!! previous email was wrong.

it turned out that your statement E=1 did not expanded in the way
Ntrials = 1, do, to

E = rep(E, n.data)

with the consequence that E was exanded into

E = c(E, NA, ...., NA)

when the first data-point is y=0 then part of the latent field will
drift to -\infty.

one might argue what E=1 means, but its reasonable that this is a
shorthand for 'all E's are 1'.

there is another issue as well, the locations of the rw2 part, pow, are
very close,

> summary(habitat2$pow)
Min. 1st Qu. Median Mean 3rd Qu. Max.
0.004491877 0.013116800 0.018262760 0.018241220 0.022909730 0.034119670


since the internal representation of the rw2 models works with these
locations, it means that the prior for the 'innovations' should be
adjusted accordingly. an easy fix is to simply do

habitat2$pow = habitat2$pow * 1000

so that

> summary(diff (sort(habitat2$pow)))
Min. 1st Qu. Median Mean 3rd Qu. Max.
0.0206190 0.1182018 0.2603405 0.4114972 0.4947525 3.6616880


is 'roughly' one in mean/median, for which the default prior makes
sense.


so this new code should run with the new build: (oops: the location of
the graph file has changed.

habitat=read.table("habitat.csv",sep=",",header=T)
head(habitat)
habitat2=cbind(habitat,region.struct=habitat$region)

habitat2$pow = habitat2$pow * 1000

formula=dens~f(region.struct,model="besag",graph.file="habitat.graph",

model=inla(formula,family="poisson",E=1,keep=T,
data=habitat2,
control.inla=list(h=0.01),
control.fixed=list(prec.intercept=.01),verbose=TRUE)
